This is why the terms 'people of colour' and 'white privilege' are very stupid.

(and divisive... perhaps intentionally)

With @Sargon_of_Akkad

Video

Most people get what they prioritise.

Unless you're pursuing something with extremely low odds, then it's rare to not attain it (in due time) if you genuinely make it a priority.

'Traditional' wisdom saves people from a lot of pain, frustration, and heartbreak.

There is a good reason why certain advice has stood the test of time for thousands of years, across cultures and nations.

You might be the exception to any given rule, but most people are not.
Happy Monday! Have an awesome week!

No es tan profundo :)


Ross Davidson (@RossDavidson7)

I'm getting real sick of people acting like Miami isn't one of the hottest US cities right now, and is instead a city for a different culture.

I live here. I don't speak Spanish. Nobody tries to talk to me in Spanish, and we all get along just fine.



— https://nitter.net/RossDavidson7/status/2048812472597901375#m

Is Miami considered part of Latin America?

And if not, why not? :)

Ok. There are definitely some crazy people, but this remains true.


ZUBY: (@ZubyMusic)

What shocks me whenever I come to the USA is how much BETTER the place and people are in real life compared to what gets amplified on social media.

This is true almost everywhere, but because so much online 'content' originates from the US, it's particularly striking.



— https://nitter.net/ZubyMusic/status/2048071770230427909#m

This is insane to me.


Tyler Todt (@tyromper)

I don't understand the boomers that hoard all their wealth from their kids.

I have a good buddy that's struggling.
Married with a few kids.

He's smart. Graduated university with great grades, got hired by a good company, & did everything "right."

He got laid off over a year ago & told me he's sent 10,000 resumes in with no job offerings.....

He's working side gigs but his family is stressed.

His folks are retired & in their 70's.

What shocks me whenever I come to the USA is how much BETTER the place and people are in real life compared to what gets amplified on social media.

This is true almost everywhere, but because so much online 'content' originates from the US, it's particularly striking.

I remember when people used to smoke on planes.

Seems like a terrible idea in hindsight.
